newsitem.title: USA: Israel to meet privatization target - trade minister.
newsitem.headline: Israel to meet privatization target - trade minister.

text.p: Israel will meet its 1997 privatization target of $1.3 billion despite some difficulties, Israel's Commerce and Industry Minister Natan Sharansky said Wednesday.
Asked about the goal, Sharansky said it would be met "for sure."
"The aim is to have $1.3 billion of privatization this year," Sharansky told reports after a luncheon here. "It's not an easy process."
He said that debates over regulation, profitability and which functions to privatize have slowed the privatization process.

The minister pointed out that about $600 million of state firms have been privatized in 1997. Israel recently auctioned about 15 percent of Bank Leumi, and plans to sell off Bank Hapoalim by year end.
"This process is absolutely irreversible," he said.
Regarding the Middle East peace process, which is currently at an impasse, Sharansky said foreign investment has not slowed from levels seen two or three years ago.
"There is no decrease in investment," he said.
The minister acknowledged that while GDP growth would slow to around 2.5 percent in 1997 and 1998, it would likely accelerate to above 4.0 percent by 2000.
